name: Beacon Events – Events Calendar with Recurring Events & Google Calendar Sync
author: beaconevents

sections.description:
Beacon Events is an events calendar for single events and repeating ones alike: a one-night workshop, a show’s run, a weekly class. It does the basics properly and doesn’t charge you for them. See it running on a stock Twenty Twenty-Five site: month grid with the filter bar, day view, event pages, venue pages.

It suits churches publishing weekly services and a monthly potluck. Yoga, pilates, fitness, dance and martial-arts studios, gyms and music schools with a weekly class schedule, shown as a timetable, and class sign-ups with Pro. Libraries and schools with story times, term dates and board meetings. Senior living communities and community centers with a monthly activity calendar that also goes up on the noticeboard. Cooking schools, paint and sip studios, pottery, glass and craft studios, art classes, makerspaces and nature centers selling workshop tickets. Wineries, breweries, taprooms and farms with tastings, beer releases, trivia nights, markets and seasonal events, and small museums with member and non-member tickets. Bars, restaurants and music venues listing live music, gigs and concerts, and a weekly happy hour. Clubs, meetups and volunteer groups, and anyone running online events on Zoom or Google Meet.

Recurring rules use the iCalendar RRULE standard, the same format Google Calendar and Outlook use, so a rule like “second Tuesday of the month” round-trips with calendar apps.

  • Recurring events are free. Daily, weekly, monthly (“second Tuesday”, “last Friday”, “the first and third Thursday”), yearly, with an end date or a count, dates you can skip, single dates you can cancel or move, and a ticket link per date when each date has its own registration page.
  • Import from Google Calendar or any ICS feed, and stay in sync. Feeds are checked hourly. Every sync is logged with what it created, updated or removed. Events that disappear from a feed are set to draft, not deleted.
  • Views that look like your site. List, photo, week, month, day and map views as blocks, shortcodes or an Elementor widget, with an optional filter bar (category, venue, search, and with “More filters” also organizer, day of the week and time of day). The week view is a class timetable: a column per day, stacked into rows on phones and narrow columns. Our stylesheet does layout only. Colours and fonts come from your theme, and every element has a class you can target. Give a category a colour and its events get a dot or a bar.
  • A month you can print. Under every month view, “Print this month” opens the month on a page of its own, laid out for one landscape sheet: times first, full titles, your category colours with a key, and the calendar’s address at the foot. Handy for a noticeboard or the front desk.
  • No bloat. Styles load only on pages that show events. No add-on store, no upsell screens, no nag notices.
  • Accessible. The month view is a real table with column headers, each day link carries its full date for screen readers, and on Twenty Twenty-Five every view passes axe-core’s automated WCAG 2.1 AA checks, colour contrast included.
  • Sell tickets where you like. Each event can link to its Eventbrite, Square or other ticket page with its own button text (“Buy on Eventbrite”, “Book now”). Or sell on the event page itself with the optional add-on, with no per-ticket fee.
  • Up and running in a minute. Click “Get started”: add a few sample events to see the calendar working (one click removes them), and let it make a Calendar page for you.
  • Every event in its own timezone. A class in Boston shows 10 am Boston time even if your site is set to Chicago, with the zone’s abbreviation when they differ. Turn on one setting and visitors in other time zones see the times in their own, for online events or for all of them.
  • Online events. Flip “Online event”, paste the meeting link, and visitors get a Join button; calendar apps get the link too.
  • Search engines understand your events. schema.org Event markup on every event page, one entry per upcoming date.
  • The details people look for. Each event can show its cost as you’d say it (“$15”, “Free”, “$10 – $20”), and its organizer with their phone, email and website. Venues have a street address with a map link (no API key, no embedded map slowing the page down) and their own phone and website. Venue and organizer pages list their events. Anything else goes in More details, a label and a value each (“Teacher: Lea Smith”, “Ages: 8 and up”).
  • Export. Every event has “Add to calendar (.ics)”, “Add to Google Calendar” and “Add to Outlook” links (Outlook.com, and Outlook for work or school accounts), and your whole calendar has a subscribable feed. Turn on “Subscribe links” on a calendar and visitors can subscribe to its events in Google Calendar, Outlook.com, Microsoft 365 or Apple Calendar in one click; category, venue and organizer pages have the same links.
  • A free alternative to The Events Calendar, Events Manager, Event Organiser, EventPrime, My Calendar, Sugar Calendar, Eventin, Modern Events Calendar, EventON, WP Event Manager, WP Events Manager (ThimPress) and All-in-One Event Calendar, and it brings your events over from any of them. Events → Import / Export copies events, venues, organizers, categories, images, recurring rules and each event’s own SEO title and description in one click, without touching the old plugin. A dry run shows first what would be created, updated or skipped, and both the dry run and the import can be downloaded as a report with one row per event. Changed your mind? Undo the import in one click, and turn the old plugin back on. Deactivate the old plugin when you are happy; old links are redirected. Weekly classes that were entered one date at a time (the only way in plugins that charge for repeating events) can be combined into one repeating event in a click. Anything else comes in through a CSV file, and every event can go out as one.
  • Uninstalls clean. Turn on “delete all data on uninstall” and the plugin removes everything it created: its events, venues, categories, settings and table.

External services

Beacon Events does not phone home or track anything, and nothing from a third party loads on your pages unless you use the map view. Three things touch the outside world, all under your control:

  • Calendar feeds you add. If you enter an ICS URL under Events → Settings (for example your Google Calendar’s public iCal address), the plugin fetches that URL from your server once an hour to keep events in sync. Nothing is fetched unless you add a feed.
  • Plain links. The “Map”, “Add to Google Calendar” and “Add to Outlook” links on an event are ordinary hyperlinks to google.com/maps, calendar.google.com, outlook.live.com and outlook.office.com. They open in the visitor’s browser; the plugin sends nothing itself. Google’s terms: https://policies.google.com/terms; Microsoft’s: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement and https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement
  • Map view (only on pages where you use it). Visitors’ browsers load map tiles from the OpenStreetMap Foundation (tile.openstreetmap.org); their tile usage policy https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/ and privacy policy https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy apply. In the venue editor, the “Find from the address” button sends that venue’s address to OpenStreetMap’s Nominatim service (https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/) when you click it; nothing is sent otherwise. The filter beacon_map_tiles switches the tile provider.

Data the plugin stores

One database table, {prefix}beacon_occurrences, holding the expanded dates of each event. It is removed on uninstall only if you turn on “delete all data on uninstall” under Events → Settings.

Shortcode

[beacon_events view="list" days="60" limit="20" category="workshops"]: `category` takes one slug or several, comma-separated (`category="workshops,talks"` shows events in either).
[beacon_events view="month"]
[beacon_events view="list" filters="1"]: adds the category / venue / search bar and a list / week / month switch.
more_filters="yes": with `filters="1"`, the bar also offers organizer, day of the week and time of day (the block's switch: "More filters").
weekdays="sat,sun" and `times="evening"`: only events on those days, or at that time of day (morning, afternoon, evening, night, allday), in the event's own time zone.
[beacon_events layout="compact" limit="5"]: one line per event, for sidebars.
[beacon_events layout="photo" limit="12"]: a card per event with its featured image (a date tile when it has none), in a grid that fits the width of the page.
[beacon_events view="map" days="90"]: upcoming events on a map, one pin per venue, with the same events listed under the map. Venues need coordinates (Events → Venues, "Find from the address"). See it on the demo: https://beacon-events.duckdns.org/demo/map/
once="1": in a list, a repeating event shows only its next date (a weekly class doesn't fill a "Coming up" box).
[beacon_events view="week"]: this week as a timetable, with previous/next links. It starts on the day set in Settings → General ("Week Starts On").
[beacon_events view="day"]: today, with previous/next links.
venue="slug" and `organizer="slug"` work like `category`.
print="no": hides the "Print this month" link under a month view.
show_venue="no": leaves the venue name off each row in a list, week or day view (the block has the same switch: "Show venue").
end_times="yes": the week and month views show each event's start and end time instead of the start time only (block switch: "Show end times").
images="yes": shows each event's featured image in a week, month or list view (the block's switch: "Show images").
subscribe="yes": adds "Subscribe: Google Calendar · Outlook.com · Microsoft 365 · Apple Calendar / Outlook app · .ics file" under the calendar, for the events it shows (the block's switch: "Subscribe links").

Block

Add the Events block and choose list, month or day in the sidebar, or the Upcoming events variation for a short one-line list. Elementor users: the Beacon Events widget has the same options.

Tickets and RSVP

Free covers the calendar. If you need people to sign up or pay, there is a paid add-on, Beacon Events Pro, with a 14-day free trial that needs no card. It adds RSVP with a capacity per date, paid tickets through Stripe or your WooCommerce checkout, a waitlist when a date is full, reminder emails the day before, attendee lists with CSV export, QR tickets with phone check-in at the door, and events your visitors submit. Nothing in the free plugin expires or nags you.

Setup in five minutes

Click Get started under the plugin’s name on the Plugins screen. The Events screen walks you through the three steps below, can add five sample events so you see a full calendar straight away (removed again in one click), and makes a “Calendar” page for you with a month view, filters and the next five events.

  1. Events → Add New Event. Set Starts and Ends in the When panel; pick Repeats if it recurs (weekly on Tuesday, second Tuesday of the month, last Friday…). Add a venue and a category from the sidebar.
  2. Put the Events block on a page (or the shortcode below). Choose list, week, month or day, and switch on the filter bar if you have several categories or venues.
  3. Moving from another plugin? Events → Import / Export. Have a Google Calendar? Events → Settings → paste its iCal address.

That is the whole setup. Everything else is optional: colours, venues with maps, online events and changes to single dates. The video at the top of this page shows these steps in 90 seconds.

Roadmap

Next, in this order: a CSV import for attendees, per-event reminder settings, and translations. Requests and bug reports on the support forum get answered; the plugin is small enough that most fixes ship within days.
sections.faq:
Are recurring events really free?

Yes. That’s the point.

How is Beacon Events different from The Events Calendar?

Recurring events and a week view: free here. In The Events Calendar the free version has month, list and day views, and recurring events and the other views come with a paid plan; the cheapest is now Liquid Web’s one-site bundle at $350 a year, or Pro alone at $399 (liquidweb.com, checked November 2026; the $259 Essentials plan is gone). Tickets: Beacon Events Pro is $7 a month, $49 a year or $149 once and sells through your own Stripe account or WooCommerce, with no per-ticket fee from us. Moving: the importer brings your events, venues, organizers, categories and repeat rules across in one click (and with Pro, tickets and attendees), and redirects the old links.

What The Events Calendar does that Beacon doesn’t, so you can decide honestly: Square and PayPal payments without WooCommerce, booking fees added to the ticket price, and add-ons such as its Event Aggregator for pulling in Eventbrite events. Discount codes are in Beacon Events Pro (Stripe promotion codes, or WooCommerce coupons at a WooCommerce checkout), and Meetup groups work here without an add-on (see the next question). If you rely on the things Beacon lacks, stay where you are.

Can I run online or hybrid events on Zoom or Google Meet?

Yes. Turn on Online event and paste the meeting link. The event page shows a “Join online” link, the calendar file carries it, and search engines are told the event is online, or online and in person when it also has a venue, with the link as its virtual location. If you’d rather not put the link on a public page, Beacon Events Pro can send it only to the people who sign up, in their confirmation and reminder emails; the event page then says the link is sent on sign-up.

Can people print the calendar?

Yes. Every month view has a “Print this month” link under the grid. It opens that month on its own page, without your theme’s header and menus, sized for one landscape sheet (a very busy month carries on to a second page), with times first, full titles, your category colours and a key to them. It prints what the view shows, so a calendar filtered to one category prints just that category. To hide the link, switch off “Print this month” link in the block’s settings, add print="no" to the shortcode, or use the beacon_print_link filter to turn it off everywhere.

Does it work on WordPress multisite?

Yes. Activate it on a single site or network-activate it; each site gets its own calendar, events and settings, and its own choice about deleting its data when the plugin is deleted. A main site can show the other sites’ events by adding their iCal feeds (each calendar has one) under Events → Settings, and they sync on a schedule.

Can I show a weekly class schedule (timetable)?

Yes. Put the Events block on a page and choose Week, or use [beacon_events view="week"]. Each day of the week gets a column with its classes in time order, all-day events first; on a phone, or in a narrow column, the days stack into rows and empty days are hidden. Enter each class once as a repeating event (“every Monday and Thursday at 6 pm”), cancel a holiday or move one class without touching the rest, and add filters="1" so visitors can pick a category (yoga, spin, kids) or a studio. Each class can carry a “Book” button to the booking system you already use.

On block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five, set the block to Wide width so all seven days fit side by side. The whole thing in 90 seconds:

Can people sign up for gym, yoga or fitness classes?

Yes, with Beacon Events Pro ($7 a month, $49 a year or $149 once). Turn on sign-ups for a class and set the places per class date, for example 25 for a spin class: each date fills up on its own, the form shows the places left, and a full class offers a waitlist that moves up when someone cancels. People get a confirmation email with a calendar file and a reminder, and can cancel themselves. Classes can be free or paid through your own Stripe account or WooCommerce, with no fee per booking on top. You see who is coming per class, print a door list or check people in with the QR code on their booking, and Pro can keep each class in your Microsoft 365 (Outlook) calendar with the names of who signed up. For a trial session or personal training, Pro splits a time into bookable slots: 60 minutes on a 9:00 to 11:00 session gives a 9:00 and a 10:00 slot, shown in the calendar as one entry or each on its own. The class timetable itself (week view with start and end times, repeating classes) is free. A sample studio timetable with sign-ups is on the demo site: https://beacon-events.duckdns.org/demo/studio/

A class set up and booked, start to finish:

Can it run a senior living community’s activity calendar?

Yes. Enter each repeating activity once (chair yoga every Monday and Wednesday, bingo on the first Friday, a birthday party on the last Thursday of the month), give each kind of activity a category colour, and put a month view on a page. Families see the calendar online, and the “Print this month” link gives staff a landscape page with the colours and a key for the noticeboard. One date can be cancelled or moved without touching the rest, and a community with several locations can give each one its own venue and let visitors filter by it.

Does it work as a church calendar?

Yes. Enter the weekly service once as a recurring event, add special services and holidays as single events, and cancel or move one date when plans change. The month view and the upcoming list go on any page, and members can add the whole calendar to their phone with the subscribe link.

Can I show my Meetup group’s events?

Yes, for free. Every Meetup group publishes its upcoming events as a calendar feed at https://www.meetup.com/your-group-name/events/ical/ (use the name from your group’s web address). Paste that address under Events → Settings → Calendar feeds. Beacon checks it every hour, so new meetups, changed times and cancellations show up on their own, each in its own time zone.

How do I connect Google Calendar?

In Google Calendar, open the calendar’s settings, make it public (“Make available to public”), and copy either its “Public address in iCal format” or its share link. Paste it under Events → Settings → Calendar feeds and save: the events come in straight away, and after that it syncs every hour (“Sync feeds now” does it on demand). webcal:// links work too. If Google ever answers with a web page instead of the calendar (say the calendar was made private), the sync stops and changes nothing, and the log says why.

I only want to show my Google Calendar on a page. Do I need all of this?

No. If the events live in Google Calendar (or Outlook or Apple Calendar) and you just want them on a page in your theme’s fonts, our separate free block Beacon Calendar Feed does only that: paste the calendar’s link into the block and it shows a list or a month without turning the events into WordPress posts. Beacon Events is for when you want the events on your own site, with their own pages, categories, venues and sign-ups.

What happens if an event is removed from my Google Calendar?

It’s set to draft on your site and the removal is written to the sync log. You decide whether to delete it.

Will it change how my site looks?

No. The stylesheet only does layout. Colours, fonts and spacing inherit from your theme.

My old calendar had every weekly class as a separate event. Can I turn them into one repeating event?

Yes. After an import (or any time), Events → Import / Export lists the events that look like one series entered date by date: same title, time, length and venue, on a regular pattern such as every Tuesday, every other Saturday, the second Tuesday of the month or three days in a row. Copies that carry their own date in the title (“Pick Your Own Project – October 1, 2026”, “Chef’s Table Class 10/2/26”) count as the same title, and the repeating event is named without the date. Tick the ones you want and click Combine. The earliest copy becomes the repeating event, a missing week becomes a skipped date, the other copies go to the trash, and their old links redirect to the new event. Events with tickets or RSVPs are left alone. From the command line: wp beacon combine --dry-run, then wp beacon combine.

Can I move my events from The Events Calendar or Events Manager?

Yes, and the migration is one click. Events → Import / Export finds what either plugin stored in your database (it works even if that plugin is already deactivated) and copies events, venues with addresses, organizers, categories, featured images, timezones and recurring rules across. Nothing is deleted. Run it again later and it updates what it imported instead of making duplicates. Old event, venue and category links are redirected to the imported items, including Events Calendar Pro’s page for each date of a series (/event/yoga/2026-10-06/), its series pages (/series/yoga/), and its week, photo, map and summary views, which go to your calendar page. Events Calendar Pro’s Additional Fields come across as More details on each event, under the same labels.

Watch the whole move, step by step (two minutes):

With Pro, tickets and attendees come across too:

Or try the whole move in your browser on a throwaway site, with nothing to install: a small site on The Events Calendar, switched off, with Beacon Events ready to import it. https://playground.wordpress.net/?blueprint-url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inmanjeffrey89-cell/beacon-events/main/blueprints/tec-move.json

My pages still have the old plugin’s shortcodes and widgets. Do they keep working?

Yes. After an import, the calendar and list shortcodes your pages used with the old plugin show Beacon Events instead of printing as text once that plugin is switched off: [tribe_events], [tribe_events_list], [tribe_mini_calendar] and [tribe_this_week] (Events Calendar Pro), [add_eventon] and [add_eventon_list] (EventON, also inside its block), [events_list] and [events_calendar] (Events Manager), [eo_events] and [eo_fullcalendar] (Event Organiser), [my_calendar], [my_calendar_upcoming] and [my_calendar_today] (My Calendar), [em_events] (EventPrime), Sugar Calendar’s, Eventin’s and WP Event Manager’s calendar and list shortcodes, ThimPress’s [wp_event_list_event], [ai1ec] and [MEC id=””]. The old month, week, day or list view is kept, and so are the category, venue, organizer and number of events when the shortcode named them. The old plugin’s sidebar widgets keep their place and title and show your upcoming events as a short list instead of disappearing, and The Events Calendar’s Elementor widgets (Events View and Events List) show Beacon’s calendar and list. While the old plugin is still active, its own shortcodes and widgets win. You can swap them for the Events block whenever it suits you.

Can I see what an import will do before it runs?

Yes. Every source under Events → Import / Export has a “Dry run first” button (wp beacon import <source> --dry-run on the command line). It goes through every event as the import would and reports what would be created, updated or skipped and why, which repeating rules would be simplified, and how many venues, organizers and categories would be added, without writing anything. Running the import again later updates instead of duplicating. The dry run and the import can both be downloaded as a CSV with one row per event (--report=file.csv on the command line).

Can I keep my old calendar plugin running while I try Beacon Events?

Yes. The Events Calendar, Events Manager, Modern Events Calendar, EventON, WP Event Manager, EventPrime, Sugar Calendar, WP Events Manager, All-in-One Event Calendar and Event Organiser use addresses that overlap with Beacon’s (/event/, /events/, /venue/ or /organizer/). While one of them is active, Beacon’s pages sit under /beacon-event/ and /beacon-events/, so your visitors keep seeing the old plugin’s pages while you look at the imported events. When you deactivate the old plugin, Beacon moves to /event/ and /events/ by itself, and links to the /beacon-… addresses are redirected.

My site already has a page called Events. Does Beacon take it over?

No. Since 0.38.3 a published page at /events/ keeps that address, so you can put the calendar block on it and that is what visitors see. Beacon’s own list of all events then lives at /beacon-events/. The same goes for a theme or plugin that already uses /event/, /venue/ or /organizer/ for its own content: those addresses stay theirs, Beacon uses /beacon-event/ and so on, and old links to Beacon’s events that the other one doesn’t know are redirected. When the page or the other post type goes away, Beacon moves back by itself.

People subscribed to my old calendar feed. Do they keep getting updates?

Yes, for The Events Calendar. After the move, its “Subscribe to calendar” address (the one Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and Outlook were given), an “Export .ics” link on any of its calendar views, its category feeds and an event’s own ?ical=1 link all answer with Beacon’s feed for the same events, so subscribed calendars keep updating. This starts once The Events Calendar is deactivated; while it is active, its own feed still answers.

Does each date of a repeating event have its own page?

Yes, since 0.39.0. Every date has its own address, /event///, that shows that date (marked if it was moved or cancelled) with a link to all dates, opens the booking form on that date when Beacon Events Pro takes bookings, and is its own page for search engines: its canonical address is itself, also with Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress, and its event data describes just that date. Google’s event results ask for a unique page for each event. The event’s main page lists the next dates, the calendar views link each repeating event to the date you clicked, and The Events Calendar Pro’s old per-date addresses now open the matching date.

Can I undo an import?

Yes. After an import, its source on Events → Import / Export shows “Undo this import”. It deletes the imported events, and the venues, organizers and categories the import created once nothing uses them. The import never changed the other plugin’s events, so turning that plugin back on brings your old calendar back as it was. Events with bookings made in Beacon are always kept, and so are events you changed after the import unless you tick the box to delete them too. On the command line: wp beacon undo <source> lists what would go, and --yes deletes it.

Can visitors see times in their own time zone?

Yes, since 0.45.0, if you want them to. Every time is written in its event’s own time zone. In Settings you can also show online events, or every event, in each visitor’s own time zone: a visitor whose clock is somewhere else sees the time converted by their browser, with the zone’s name (“8:30 AM GMT+9”) and a line saying so, and the event’s own time stays as the tooltip. A time that falls on another day for them names that day, and an event page adds a “Your time” line. Visitors in your own time zone see nothing different. All-day events stay as they are.

Do my events keep their SEO titles and descriptions?

Yes, since 0.44.0. When events move in from The Events Calendar or any of the other plugins Beacon imports from, each event’s own SEO settings come along: the custom title, meta description, focus keyword, robots and canonical settings and social titles from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress, The SEO Framework and All in One SEO. The old plugin’s primary-category choice and its per-event schema stay behind, because they point at that plugin’s categories and Beacon writes its own Event markup. The dry run tells you how many events have their own SEO settings, per SEO plugin. A CSV import has no old post, so there is nothing to bring.

Can I move my events from Sugar Calendar?

Yes, from Sugar Calendar Lite or Pro, active or already deactivated. Events → Import / Export copies events with their times and timezones, all-day and multi-day events, locations with their addresses (as venues), calendars (as categories with their colours), featured images, online events with their links, and repeats (daily, weekly, every other week, monthly, yearly) with their end date or count. Joining links Sugar Calendar showed to attendees only stay off the public page; the import report lists them. Its old /events/… and calendar links redirect to the imported ones.

Can I move my events from My Calendar?

Yes, active or already deactivated. Events → Import / Export reads My Calendar’s tables and copies events with their times, all-day events, locations with their addresses, categories with their colours, descriptions, featured images and the ticket or event link (it becomes the “Tickets & info” button). A repeating event becomes one repeating event, checked against every date My Calendar stored, so a date you deleted stays deleted; dates that fit no rule are listed in the report. Its old event, location and category pages and ?mc_id= links redirect to the imported ones.

Can I move my events from EventPrime?

Yes, active or already deactivated. Events → Import / Export copies events with their times, all-day events, venues with their addresses, event types (as categories with their colours), organizers, featured images and the outside booking link (it becomes the “Tickets & info” button). A repeating event becomes one repeating event, checked against every date EventPrime made; hand-picked dates and “advanced” repeats come over as one event per date, which Combine can join later. Bookings and tickets are not imported. Its old ?event= links and SEO addresses redirect to the imported ones.

Can I move my events from Event Organiser?

Yes, active or already deactivated. Events → Import / Export copies events with their times, all-day events, venues with their addresses, categories with their colours, featured images and descriptions. Repeats keep their schedule: the rule is rebuilt from Event Organiser’s settings and checked against every date it saved, so skipped dates stay skipped. A schedule no rule can describe comes over on its first date, and the report lists the other dates. Tags are not imported. Its old event, venue and category links redirect to the imported ones.

Can I move my events from Eventin?

Yes, active or already deactivated. Events → Import / Export copies events with their times and timezones, multi-day events, locations with their addresses, categories, featured images, and online and hybrid events. A repeating series becomes one repeating event when Beacon can repeat the same dates exactly; hand-picked dates come over as one event per date, which Combine can join later. Meeting links stay off public pages (the report lists them), and Eventin’s sample events are left out. Its /etn/… links redirect to the imported events.

Can I move my events from EventON?

Yes, from EventON or EventON Lite, active or already deactivated. Events → Import / Export copies events with their times and timezones, all-day events, locations with their addresses, organizers, event types (as categories, with the event’s colour), featured images, “moved online” join links and repeats. EventON saves every date a repeat makes, and the importer keeps a rule only when it makes exactly those dates; otherwise the first date comes across and the report names the event. Its old /events/…, /event-location/…, /event-organizer/… and /event-type/… links redirect.

Can I move my events from WP Event Manager?

Yes, active or already deactivated. Events → Import / Export copies events (expired ones as past events), venues with the address from each event, organizers, categories and event types (as categories), featured images or banners, per-event timezones and the online flag. Its /event/… and /event-category/… links already match Beacon’s, and /event-type/… links redirect. Ticket sales and registrations from its paid add-ons are not imported; the ticket type and price stay on each event for reference.

Can I move my events from Modern Events Calendar (MEC)?

Yes, from MEC Lite or Pro, active or already deactivated. Events → Import / Export copies events, venues with their addresses, organizers, categories with their colours, featured images, timezones, “moved online” join links and repeats (daily, weekly, weekdays, weekends, monthly, yearly, “first/last weekday of the month”) with their end and skipped dates. The report names two partial cases: a hand-picked list of dates imports its first date, and a month rule with several weekdays keeps the first. MEC bookings are not imported. Its old event and category links redirect, custom slugs included.

Can I move my events from WP Events Manager by ThimPress?

Yes, with the ThimPress plugin (it comes with themes like Eduma) active or already deactivated. Events → Import / Export copies events with their times (older date formats too), all-day and multi-day events, the location as a venue, categories and event types, featured images and past events. Tags are not imported. Its old /events/…, /tp-event-category/… and /tp-event-type/… links redirect. Seats and price stay on each event; Beacon Events Pro turns them into tickets and imports completed bookings as attendees, with no emails sent.

All-in-One Event Calendar (Time.ly) was removed from wordpress.org. Can I move my events?

Yes. AI1EC’s events stay in your database, and Events → Import / Export reads them directly, even with All-in-One Event Calendar still active or already deactivated. Events, categories with their colours, venues with addresses, contacts, featured images, timezones, recurring rules and skipped dates come across; “every weekday” rules become a weekly rule on those days. Events it pulled in from calendar feeds keep their feed IDs, so adding the same feed under Events → Settings adopts them instead of duplicating them. Its old category and calendar-view links are redirected, and the report tells you which page used to show the calendar.

What about my tickets and attendees from Event Tickets or Event Tickets Plus?

The free importer moves events, venues, organizers and categories, and shows how many tickets and confirmed attendees it found. Beacon Events Pro, the paid add-on, imports those too: each event’s ticket price and capacity, every RSVP “yes”, every attendee of a completed Tickets Commerce order, and every Event Tickets Plus attendee whose WooCommerce order is completed or processing, with the order linked. Unpaid orders are left behind and no emails are sent.

Can I run the import from the command line?

Yes, with WP-CLI, which helps when you are moving several sites. wp beacon sources lists what it finds from each supported plugin, and wp beacon import tec (or em, ai1ec, mec, wpem, eventon, wpems) runs the same import as the Import / Export screen, with a progress bar and the same report. Beacon Events Pro’s ticket and attendee import runs too when it is active. Running it again updates instead of duplicating.

Can I import from a spreadsheet?

Yes. Save it as CSV with a header row (title and start are the only required columns; venue, address, organizer, categories, repeat rule, skip dates, online link, image URL and cost are optional) and upload it on Events → Import / Export. Export gives you every event in the same format, and an edited export comes back as updates.

Can I cancel or move just one date of a recurring event?

Yes. Under the rule in the editor sidebar (or the When box in the classic editor) the next few dates are listed; mark one cancelled and it stays on the calendar as cancelled, or move it to another time. Skipped dates, by contrast, disappear entirely.

Each date of my program has its own registration page (Blackbaud, Altru, Eventbrite). Can it still be one repeating event?

Yes. Every upcoming date in the editor has a “Ticket link for this date” box. The list view links each date to its own page, the event page lists the next dates with their links, and calendar files carry them too. When you combine events that were entered one date at a time, each date keeps the link it had, whether it was the event’s website link or a “click here to register” link in its description.

Can I sell tickets for cooking classes, paint and sip nights or workshops?

Yes, with Beacon Events Pro. Each class gets a capacity so it shows sold out on its own, a waitlist, and ticket types such as member and non-member prices. Buyers pay through your own Stripe account or your WooCommerce checkout, and every ticket has a QR code.

Is there a ticket scanner for check-in at the door?

Yes, in Beacon Events Pro. Every ticket email links to a ticket page with a QR code. Scan it with your phone’s own camera while logged in to your site and the guest is checked in, with a clear warning if the ticket was already used or cancelled. No separate app is needed, and you can also print a door list.

Can an event link to tickets I sell somewhere else, like Eventbrite or Square?

Yes. Every event has an optional “Tickets & info” link with its own button text (“Buy on Eventbrite”, “Book on Square”, “Register”). It shows as a button on the event page, next to the event in lists, and in the calendar feed. When you import from The Events Calendar, All-in-One Event Calendar, Modern Events Calendar, EventON or WP Event Manager, the ticket or website link each event had comes across as this button, so nothing your visitors clicked goes missing.

Can I sell tickets without Eventbrite’s per-ticket fees?

Yes, with Beacon Events Pro, as an Eventbrite alternative for tickets you sell from your own site. Buyers pay through your own Stripe account or your WooCommerce checkout, so the only fee is your payment provider’s card fee. Eventbrite’s US pricing adds a service fee of 3.7% + $1.79 to every paid ticket. Pro is $7 a month, $49 a year or $149 once for one site and includes a capacity per date, a waitlist, reminder emails, an attendee list, QR tickets you scan at the door with a phone, and a printable door list. Each event can have several ticket types, like early bird and VIP, with their own prices and capacities. There is no reserved seating, so it suits classes, workshops and small events.

What’s in the paid version?

Tickets and RSVPs with card payments, attendee export, and priority support. You can try it free for 14 days without a card. Nothing in the free version moves behind a paywall.

Every event page says “Page not found”

WordPress keeps a saved list of link rules, and sometimes another plugin, a cache or a site move saves it without Beacon’s. Since 0.29.3 Beacon rebuilds it by itself the next time someone opens an event. On older versions, or if it keeps happening, go to Settings → Permalinks and click Save Changes (no need to change anything). If event pages still 404 after that, another plugin is using /event/ for its own pages.

Are my events in my SEO plugin’s sitemap?

WordPress’s own sitemap lists them by itself. Rank Math stores an “include in sitemap” switch for each kind of content only when it is first set up, so on a site that got Beacon Events later it left every event out, even though its settings showed the switch as on. Since 0.37.0 Beacon reads that missing switch as on; if you turned it off in Rank Math, it stays off. SEOPress lists only the post types you tick, so tick Events in its XML sitemap settings.

My theme’s event page doesn’t show the date, place or booking form

Some themes and theme builders draw single pages with their own template. Since 0.28.1 Beacon adds its When / Where box (and Pro’s booking form) there too. If your template leaves the page content out entirely, put the [beacon_event_details] shortcode in it (and [beacon_rsvp] for Pro’s booking form).

Is Beacon Events translated?

German is included (since 0.28.0) and loads by itself on a German site. Every other language can be added at translate.wordpress.org/projects/wp-plugins/beacon-events/, and a finished translation arrives as a normal update.

Can club leaders or volunteers add events without being able to write blog posts?

Yes. Give them the “Event organizer” role (Users → Edit user → Role). They can add, publish and edit their own events, pick categories, add a venue and upload images, but they can’t write posts or pages or change anyone else’s events, and they land on their events list when they log in. Other roles keep what they have with posts: Authors publish their own events, Contributors submit theirs for review, Editors edit everyone’s. With a role editor plugin you can fine-tune it, for example take “publish_beacon_events” away so their events wait for review.
sections.changelog:
0.57.0

  • New map view: [beacon_events view=”map”], or View → Map on the Events block and the Elementor widget, shows upcoming events on a map with one pin per venue, and lists the same events under the map. Leaflet is bundled with the plugin; map tiles come from OpenStreetMap, and only on pages that show a map.
  • Venues get Latitude and Longitude fields and a “Find from the address” button, which asks OpenStreetMap’s Nominatim service for the coordinates when you click it.

0.56.0

  • New photo view: [beacon_events layout=”photo”], or Layout → Photo on the Events block and the Elementor widget, shows upcoming events as cards with their featured image, or a date tile when an event has none.
  • FAQ: how to show a Meetup group’s events with its calendar feed.

0.55.3

  • Plainer wording on the Tickets & RSVP page and on this plugin page. No changes to how anything works.

0.55.2

  • The Plugins screen links to the Tickets & RSVP page, so you can see what the paid add-on does without hunting for it. The link goes away once Pro is installed.
  • When an event’s “Tickets & info” link points at a ticketing site such as Eventbrite, the editor mentions once, under that field, that Pro can take bookings on the event page instead. Still no admin notices anywhere.

0.55.1

  • With “Show end times” on, a narrow week or month cell no longer leaves “am” or “pm” alone on the next line: a time range wraps only after the dash.
  • Booking add-ons can now show one date as several calendar entries (filter beacon_view_rows). Beacon Events Pro uses it to show bookable time slots on their own, for example 9:00 – 10:00 and 10:00 – 11:00. Thanks to TopFit for asking.

0.55.0

  • New “Show end times” switch for the week and month views (end_times=”yes” for the shortcode): each event shows its start and end time, like 9:00 – 10:00, instead of the start time only. Thanks to TopFit for asking.

0.54.0

  • New “More filters” switch for the Events block’s filter bar (more_filters=”yes” for the shortcode): visitors can also pick an organizer, a day of the week and a time of day (morning, afternoon, evening, night or all-day events). These are the filters most sites set up in The Events Calendar’s paid Filter Bar add-on, and a site that had Filter Bar gets them on its old calendar shortcodes and on the calendar page Beacon creates. The picks stay in the address, so a filtered view can be shared or printed.
  • The shortcode takes weekdays=”sat,sun” and times=”evening” to limit a calendar the same way without the bar.

0.53.0

  • New: More details on events. Add rows with a label and a value (“Teacher: Lea Smith”, “Ages: 8 and up”) in the When panel or the classic editor box; they show on the event page with the other details. A web address becomes a link.
  • The Events Calendar importer brings Events Calendar Pro’s Additional Fields across as More details, labelled the same, with checkbox choices joined and website fields as links. The CSV import and export carry them in a “details” column.
  • Duplicate keeps text with quotes in it intact in the copy’s details and per-date changes.

0.52.0

  • The Map link searches Google Maps for the venue’s real name; names with “&” were sent as “&”.
  • An organizer with the same name as the event’s venue and no contact details of its own isn’t listed again under Organizer (a venue that runs its own events).
  • The Subscribe links wrap on narrow screens instead of running off the side (seen on Twenty Twenty-One’s venue pages on phones).
  • The sample events show a price and an organizer, so a first look at the calendar shows those fields too.
  • An event’s old address from before it was combined into a repeating event now redirects while another calendar plugin is still active too (Beacon’s addresses then start with /beacon-event/).

0.51.0

  • The import summary counts in the right number (“1 new event”, “1 organizer and 1 category”); it said “1 organizers” before.

0.50.0

  • Venues have a phone and website, and organizers a phone, email and website (Events → Venues / Organizers). The event page shows them under “Where” and in a new “Organizer” row, with each organizer linked to their own page, and venue and organizer pages show them too. Email addresses are written so that address-harvesting bots can’t read them.
  • Moving in from The Events Calendar brings its venues’ phone and website and its organizers’ phone, email, website and description along; from Modern Events Calendar, its organizers’ phone, email and website and its locations’ website. A re-import never overwrites details you’ve filled in yourself.

0.49.0

  • Events have a Cost field: write what it costs the way you’d say it (“$15”, “Free”, “$10 – $20”) and it shows on the event page and in list views. Set it in the event’s When panel (or the classic box), or with a “cost” column in a CSV import.
  • Moving in from The Events Calendar, Modern Events Calendar or All-in-One Event Calendar now brings each event’s cost into that field, with the old plugin’s currency symbol (“$15”, “25 €”, 0 as “Free”), instead of listing it as a field Beacon doesn’t show.

0.48.0

  • New “Subscribe links” switch for the Events block (and subscribe=”yes” for the shortcode): under the calendar, one line lets visitors subscribe to its events in Google Calendar, Outlook.com, Microsoft 365, Apple Calendar or the Outlook app, or download the .ics file. The feed follows the calendar’s own category, venue and organizer limits. Off by default.
  • Category, venue and organizer pages now offer the same subscribe links instead of only the .ics file.
  • Moved from The Events Calendar? Its [tribe_events] calendars showed a “Subscribe to calendar” menu, and after the move they show these links in its place.
  • The calendar feed now takes several categories, venues or organizers (?beacon_category=a,b): events in any of them.

Older versions: see changelog.txt.

short_description: Free events calendar for one-off and recurring events, with Google Calendar sync and one-click import from The Events Calendar or Events Manager.
description:
Beacon Events is an events calendar for single events and repeating ones alike: a one-night workshop, a show’s run, a weekly class. It does the basics properly and doesn’t charge you for them. See it running on a stock Twenty Twenty-Five site: month grid with the filter bar, day view, event pages, venue pages.

It suits churches publishing weekly services and a monthly potluck. Yoga, pilates, fitness, dance and martial-arts studios, gyms and music schools with a weekly class schedule, shown as a timetable, and class sign-ups with Pro. Libraries and schools with story times, term dates and board meetings. Senior living communities and community centers with a monthly activity calendar that also goes up on the noticeboard. Cooking schools, paint and sip studios, pottery, glass and craft studios, art classes, makerspaces and nature centers selling workshop tickets. Wineries, breweries, taprooms and farms with tastings, beer releases, trivia nights, markets and seasonal events, and small museums with member and non-member tickets. Bars, restaurants and music venues listing live music, gigs and concerts, and a weekly happy hour. Clubs, meetups and volunteer groups, and anyone running online events on Zoom or Google Meet.

Recurring rules use the iCalendar RRULE standard, the same format Google Calendar and Outlook use, so a rule like “second Tuesday of the month” round-trips with calendar apps.

  • Recurring events are free. Daily, weekly, monthly (“second Tuesday”, “last Friday”, “the first and third Thursday”), yearly, with an end date or a count, dates you can skip, single dates you can cancel or move, and a ticket link per date when each date has its own registration page.
  • Import from Google Calendar or any ICS feed, and stay in sync. Feeds are checked hourly. Every sync is logged with what it created, updated or removed. Events that disappear from a feed are set to draft, not deleted.
  • Views that look like your site. List, photo, week, month, day and map views as blocks, shortcodes or an Elementor widget, with an optional filter bar (category, venue, search, and with “More filters” also organizer, day of the week and time of day). The week view is a class timetable: a column per day, stacked into rows on phones and narrow columns. Our stylesheet does layout only. Colours and fonts come from your theme, and every element has a class you can target. Give a category a colour and its events get a dot or a bar.
  • A month you can print. Under every month view, “Print this month” opens the month on a page of its own, laid out for one landscape sheet: times first, full titles, your category colours with a key, and the calendar’s address at the foot. Handy for a noticeboard or the front desk.
  • No bloat. Styles load only on pages that show events. No add-on store, no upsell screens, no nag notices.
  • Accessible. The month view is a real table with column headers, each day link carries its full date for screen readers, and on Twenty Twenty-Five every view passes axe-core’s automated WCAG 2.1 AA checks, colour contrast included.
  • Sell tickets where you like. Each event can link to its Eventbrite, Square or other ticket page with its own button text (“Buy on Eventbrite”, “Book now”). Or sell on the event page itself with the optional add-on, with no per-ticket fee.
  • Up and running in a minute. Click “Get started”: add a few sample events to see the calendar working (one click removes them), and let it make a Calendar page for you.
  • Every event in its own timezone. A class in Boston shows 10 am Boston time even if your site is set to Chicago, with the zone’s abbreviation when they differ. Turn on one setting and visitors in other time zones see the times in their own, for online events or for all of them.
  • Online events. Flip “Online event”, paste the meeting link, and visitors get a Join button; calendar apps get the link too.
  • Search engines understand your events. schema.org Event markup on every event page, one entry per upcoming date.
  • The details people look for. Each event can show its cost as you’d say it (“$15”, “Free”, “$10 – $20”), and its organizer with their phone, email and website. Venues have a street address with a map link (no API key, no embedded map slowing the page down) and their own phone and website. Venue and organizer pages list their events. Anything else goes in More details, a label and a value each (“Teacher: Lea Smith”, “Ages: 8 and up”).
  • Export. Every event has “Add to calendar (.ics)”, “Add to Google Calendar” and “Add to Outlook” links (Outlook.com, and Outlook for work or school accounts), and your whole calendar has a subscribable feed. Turn on “Subscribe links” on a calendar and visitors can subscribe to its events in Google Calendar, Outlook.com, Microsoft 365 or Apple Calendar in one click; category, venue and organizer pages have the same links.
  • A free alternative to The Events Calendar, Events Manager, Event Organiser, EventPrime, My Calendar, Sugar Calendar, Eventin, Modern Events Calendar, EventON, WP Event Manager, WP Events Manager (ThimPress) and All-in-One Event Calendar, and it brings your events over from any of them. Events → Import / Export copies events, venues, organizers, categories, images, recurring rules and each event’s own SEO title and description in one click, without touching the old plugin. A dry run shows first what would be created, updated or skipped, and both the dry run and the import can be downloaded as a report with one row per event. Changed your mind? Undo the import in one click, and turn the old plugin back on. Deactivate the old plugin when you are happy; old links are redirected. Weekly classes that were entered one date at a time (the only way in plugins that charge for repeating events) can be combined into one repeating event in a click. Anything else comes in through a CSV file, and every event can go out as one.
  • Uninstalls clean. Turn on “delete all data on uninstall” and the plugin removes everything it created: its events, venues, categories, settings and table.

External services

Beacon Events does not phone home or track anything, and nothing from a third party loads on your pages unless you use the map view. Three things touch the outside world, all under your control:

  • Calendar feeds you add. If you enter an ICS URL under Events → Settings (for example your Google Calendar’s public iCal address), the plugin fetches that URL from your server once an hour to keep events in sync. Nothing is fetched unless you add a feed.
  • Plain links. The “Map”, “Add to Google Calendar” and “Add to Outlook” links on an event are ordinary hyperlinks to google.com/maps, calendar.google.com, outlook.live.com and outlook.office.com. They open in the visitor’s browser; the plugin sends nothing itself. Google’s terms: https://policies.google.com/terms; Microsoft’s: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement and https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement
  • Map view (only on pages where you use it). Visitors’ browsers load map tiles from the OpenStreetMap Foundation (tile.openstreetmap.org); their tile usage policy https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/ and privacy policy https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy apply. In the venue editor, the “Find from the address” button sends that venue’s address to OpenStreetMap’s Nominatim service (https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/) when you click it; nothing is sent otherwise. The filter beacon_map_tiles switches the tile provider.

Data the plugin stores

One database table, {prefix}beacon_occurrences, holding the expanded dates of each event. It is removed on uninstall only if you turn on “delete all data on uninstall” under Events → Settings.

Shortcode

[beacon_events view="list" days="60" limit="20" category="workshops"]: `category` takes one slug or several, comma-separated (`category="workshops,talks"` shows events in either).
[beacon_events view="month"]
[beacon_events view="list" filters="1"]: adds the category / venue / search bar and a list / week / month switch.
more_filters="yes": with `filters="1"`, the bar also offers organizer, day of the week and time of day (the block's switch: "More filters").
weekdays="sat,sun" and `times="evening"`: only events on those days, or at that time of day (morning, afternoon, evening, night, allday), in the event's own time zone.
[beacon_events layout="compact" limit="5"]: one line per event, for sidebars.
[beacon_events layout="photo" limit="12"]: a card per event with its featured image (a date tile when it has none), in a grid that fits the width of the page.
[beacon_events view="map" days="90"]: upcoming events on a map, one pin per venue, with the same events listed under the map. Venues need coordinates (Events → Venues, "Find from the address"). See it on the demo: https://beacon-events.duckdns.org/demo/map/
once="1": in a list, a repeating event shows only its next date (a weekly class doesn't fill a "Coming up" box).
[beacon_events view="week"]: this week as a timetable, with previous/next links. It starts on the day set in Settings → General ("Week Starts On").
[beacon_events view="day"]: today, with previous/next links.
venue="slug" and `organizer="slug"` work like `category`.
print="no": hides the "Print this month" link under a month view.
show_venue="no": leaves the venue name off each row in a list, week or day view (the block has the same switch: "Show venue").
end_times="yes": the week and month views show each event's start and end time instead of the start time only (block switch: "Show end times").
images="yes": shows each event's featured image in a week, month or list view (the block's switch: "Show images").
subscribe="yes": adds "Subscribe: Google Calendar · Outlook.com · Microsoft 365 · Apple Calendar / Outlook app · .ics file" under the calendar, for the events it shows (the block's switch: "Subscribe links").

Block

Add the Events block and choose list, month or day in the sidebar, or the Upcoming events variation for a short one-line list. Elementor users: the Beacon Events widget has the same options.

Tickets and RSVP

Free covers the calendar. If you need people to sign up or pay, there is a paid add-on, Beacon Events Pro, with a 14-day free trial that needs no card. It adds RSVP with a capacity per date, paid tickets through Stripe or your WooCommerce checkout, a waitlist when a date is full, reminder emails the day before, attendee lists with CSV export, QR tickets with phone check-in at the door, and events your visitors submit. Nothing in the free plugin expires or nags you.

Setup in five minutes

Click Get started under the plugin’s name on the Plugins screen. The Events screen walks you through the three steps below, can add five sample events so you see a full calendar straight away (removed again in one click), and makes a “Calendar” page for you with a month view, filters and the next five events.

  1. Events → Add New Event. Set Starts and Ends in the When panel; pick Repeats if it recurs (weekly on Tuesday, second Tuesday of the month, last Friday…). Add a venue and a category from the sidebar.
  2. Put the Events block on a page (or the shortcode below). Choose list, week, month or day, and switch on the filter bar if you have several categories or venues.
  3. Moving from another plugin? Events → Import / Export. Have a Google Calendar? Events → Settings → paste its iCal address.

That is the whole setup. Everything else is optional: colours, venues with maps, online events and changes to single dates. The video at the top of this page shows these steps in 90 seconds.

Roadmap

Next, in this order: a CSV import for attendees, per-event reminder settings, and translations. Requests and bug reports on the support forum get answered; the plugin is small enough that most fixes ship within days.
